newsitem.title: FINLAND: Small-cap muscle boosts Helsinki, Nokia firms.
newsitem.headline: Small-cap muscle boosts Helsinki, Nokia firms.

text.p: Shares rose on Thursday on a small-caps rally led by Santasalo which hit a life-high on its purchase of Asko's components unit, brokers said.
The HEX index index put on 0.58 percent to end at 2,712.23 with bourse engine Nokia recovering from Wednesday's weakness, adding 2.50 markka to 307.00 in over 40 percent of total trade.

Forestries were under pressure after Swedish rivals SCA and Stora said little in their 1996 reports to encourage hopes for a long-awaited upturn, but losses were capped ahead of Finnish reports with the sub-index down 0.50 percent, brokers said.
Santasalo jumped 3.50 markka or over seven percent to close at a new 52.00 all-time-high.
"The market received the news of Santasalo's acquisition very well," one broker said.
Hardware and car retailer Starckjohann extended recent gains to close up almost 12 percent at 9.55 markka in relatively massive 46 million markka trade.

"I've been on the block with Starckjohann all day and it has been laudably lively," one broker said, adding four brokerages had issued buy recommendations on the stock based on its improving fundamentals and the construction sector outlook.
"Starckjohann is still in debt restructuring, but it is expected to be able to get out of that situation soon. At P/E's less than 10, it has been seen attractive," said another.
